mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen every week for the past four weeks (-73.0 to -59.0 to -52.3 to -37.6), an average gain of about 11.8 points per week. This momentum reflects an ongoing recovery trajectory that is expected to continue into the next four weeks, producing a higher mean RETAIL_REC than the prior 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC increased in each of the last three weekly observations
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than its mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined steadily from 24.6 to 14.9 over four weeks, indicating people are spending progressively less time at home. Once RESIDENTIAL falls below the 15-point threshold, the freed-up time is expected to translate into increased discretionary outings, raising RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 15 points for the current week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at t-0w is 14.9, already near the 15-point threshold
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below 15 but RETAIL_REC does not rise, or declines, over the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT have both risen concurrently each week (WORKPLACES -56.3 to -37.3; TRANSIT -61.1 to -44.3). Joint recovery of commuting-linked mobility signals restoration of weekday routines that generate incidental retail trips (lunch breaks, after-work errands), pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks when both series continue co-rising.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase by at least 5 points week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:both series rose in each of the last three weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise concurrently for two or more weeks but RETAIL_REC growth stalls or reverses over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has flipped from -20.9 to +19.3 over four weeks, consistent with warmer summer weather drawing people outdoors. This seasonal outdoor-activity surge is expected to spill over into adjacent retail and recreation spending (terraces, outdoor dining, shopping on the way to parks), raising RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS turned positive at t-2w and continued rising to 19.3 by t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS continues to rise but RETAIL_REC fails to increase in parallel over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility is nearly at the -45 threshold (-44.3 at t-0w), suggesting imminent easing of public-transit capacity restrictions under the phased reopening policy. Crossing this threshold is expected to enable greater access to retail districts via public transport, raising RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -45 (i.e., becomes less negative than -45)
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at t-0w equals -44.3, just above the -45 threshold
failure_condition: TRANSIT crosses above -45 but RETAIL_REC decreases or stays flat in the following week.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM (-26.4 to -10.0) and RESIDENTIAL (24.6 to 14.9) are both converging toward their pre-pandemic baselines simultaneously, indicating a joint behavioral normalization: less precautionary stockpiling and less home confinement. This combined normalization frees both time and spending capacity for discretionary retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM is between -15 and 0 and RESIDENTIAL is below 15 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both series show monotonic convergence toward baseline over the last four weeks
failure_condition: Both GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL normalize per the trigger criteria but RETAIL_REC plateaus or declines over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: As RETAIL_REC approaches its pre-pandemic baseline, the weekly point-gain should shrink due to diminishing room for further recovery (saturation effect). If the weekly increment falls below 5 points for two consecutive weeks, this signals the recovery trend is losing steam and the near-term trajectory will flatten or reverse within the next week.
candidate_trigger: weekly increment of RETAIL_REC falls below 5 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:weekly increments have been 14.0, 6.7, and 14.7 points, showing volatility rather than monotonic deceleration yet
failure_condition: Despite two consecutive weeks of sub-5-point increments, RETAIL_REC's next 4-week mean is still higher than its prior 4-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained rise in WORKPLACES (-56.3 to -37.3 over four weeks) reflects an active phased reopening policy progressively lifting restrictions on commercial and office activity. As long as this reopening regime persists, continued WORKPLACES gains are expected to coincide with and drive further RETAIL_REC increases over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES increased in each of the last three weekly observations
failure_condition: WORKPLACES continues to rise across the next four weeks but RETAIL_REC's mean does not increase relative to the prior 28 days.
